package.title: How Conan Doyle Invented The Mary Celeste Myth

scenes.narration: You probably know the story of the abandoned ghost ship Mary Celeste.

visuals.ai_prompt: Cinematic vertical shot of an old sailing ship at sea, dramatic lighting.

scenes.narration: But its most famous details are complete fiction.

visuals.ai_prompt: Cinematic vertical shot of rough ocean waves.

scenes.narration: In 1884, a young Arthur Conan Doyle published a fictional story about the ship.

visuals.ai_prompt: Portrait of a 19th-century writer at a desk.

scenes.narration: He even misspelled the name as Marie Celeste, cementing the error in the public mind.

visuals.ai_prompt: Close up of old book pages with handwritten text.

scenes.narration: A great story often overshadows history. Follow for more strange truths.

visuals.ai_prompt: Cinematic vertical shot of a foggy ocean horizon at sunset.

package.description: How Arthur Conan Doyle accidentally created the enduring myth of the ghost ship Mary Celeste through a fictional story.

sources.title: Mary Celeste - Wikipedia
sources.used_for: Core details on Arthur Conan Doyle and the naming myth

claims.claim: Arthur Conan Doyle published a fictional short story about the ship in 1884 that popularized the Marie Celeste spelling.
